qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Proprietary high-performance polyamide compounding (EMS-Grivory) and automotive OEM co-development specifications create significant switching costs. Historical ROIC of 23-28% and ~27% EBIT margins provide empirical proof of moat, though auto OEM customer concentration poses erosion threats.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While EMS-Chemie possesses high ROIC and disciplined family ownership, ~60%+ direct exposure to global automotive manufacturing faces severe terminal headwinds from European auto de-industrialization, shift to Chinese EV ecosystems, and commoditization pressure from rival polyamide producers.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-year ROIC averages ~25-28% with operating margins around 26-28% and pristine net-cash balance sheet. However, over 60% of revenue stems from automotive applications (Grivory metal replacement and EFTEC adhesives). European automotive volume stagnation and aggressive Asian competition limit predictable competitive advantage period to well below the 15-year threshold.
